top news.title: Sources: Stripe and PE firm Advent have jointly offered $60.50/share to acquire PayPal, a 28% premium to Tuesday's close, valuing it at $53B+; PYPL jumps 17.2%

tweets.author: @dadiomov
tweets.text: Every experience I've had across Stripe and PayPal suggests that it would be a monstrously difficult culture clash to attempt to combine.  Smart to have Advent involved in operating it at arms' length.  But it does beg the question of what parts of PayPal would go “into” Stripe to make it all worthwhile.

tweets.author: @jason
tweets.text: A Startup Is Trying to Buy PayPal — Craziest Deal of 2026!

tweets.author: @iankar_
tweets.text: Stripe buying PayPal and taking it private would be great. Put it out of its misery. Would give a huge boost to Stripe for in store payments and consumer via Venmo.

top news.title: Thinking Machines Lab debuts Inkling, an open-weight MoE model with 975B total and 41B active parameters, trained to be broad rather than optimized for one area

tweets.author: @natolambert
tweets.text: Pretty detailed safety section of model card, I found this interesting and practical: “Across all areas, we concluded that Inkling did not present risk of material uplift beyond what's already available in the open-weight ecosystem.”

tweets.author: @mweinbach
tweets.text: This model is interesting because it's the seemingly best base for a full scale post train/RL run for specific workloads or generalization. Helps that it's audio/image/text in! I'd be curious to see a proper model built off this or how Thinking Machine customers use it

tweets.author: @designarena
tweets.text: BREAKING: Inkling by @thinkymachines is 9th overall on Agentic Web App Arena by Design Arena with an Elo of 1257 It's an open-weight model in the same performance band as Claude Opus 4.6 by @AnthropicAI and Gemini 3.5 Flash by @GoogleDeepMind This makes Inkling the highest-ranking US-based open-weight model for agentic workloads, achieving frontier-level performance Congrats to the @thinkymachines team for this achievement!

top news.title: China says Apple Intelligence has been registered for use on iPhones in the country; the service will integrate Alibaba's Qwen and may add Baidu's AI features

tweets.author: @markgurman
tweets.text: After two years of regulatory delays, Apple Intelligence was finally approved by the Chinese government. No word yet on when a launch will happen - but Apple could flick this on server-side. This is separate from Siri AI.

tweets.author: @stocksavvyshay
tweets.text: $AAPL on-device AI has reportedly received approval for iPhones in China. $BABA says Qwen will power Apple Intelligence across iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS for Chinese users. [image]
